question: An electric heater of resistance 20Ω operates for 10 minutes when connected to a 220 V supply. The heat produced is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**1.45 × 10⁶ J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The heat produced in an electric heater is calculated using **Joule's Law of Heating**: **H = (V²/R) × t**
 
• Given:
 
 
• Voltage, **V = 220 V**
 
• Resistance, **R = 20 Ω**
 
• Time, **t = 10 minutes = 600 s**
 
 
 
• Substituting the values:

 **H = (220²/20) × 600**

 **= (48400/20) × 600**

 **= 2420 × 600**

 **= 1,452,000 J**

 **= 1.452 × 10⁶ J**
 
• ***Hence, the heat produced is 1.45 × 10⁶ J.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joule's Law of Heating:**

 
 
• **H = I²Rt**
 
• **H = VIt**
 
• **H = (V²/R)t**
 
• All three expressions are equivalent.
 
 
 
• **SI Unit of Heat Energy:**
 
 
• The SI unit is the **joule (J)**.
 
 
 
• **Electric Power:**
 
 
• **P = VI = I²R = V²/R**.
 
• For this heater, **P = 2420 W**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Joule Heating:**
 
 
• Electric heaters
 
• Electric irons
 
• Toasters
 
• Electric kettles
